findings.reason: The protected source is a compact zero-or-one subset-sum dynamic program encoded as a packed bitset. Its total, target, reachable, and value concepts expose the reduction and state transition directly, with no unnecessary machinery. No candidate is justified.

Metadata consistently identifies public LeetCode problem 416 and its Python canPartition surface. The Reference preserves complete two-subset partitioning, equal-sum semantics, both source examples with complete explanations, and both source constraints.

The immutable native source remains tied to verified submission 2064749079. Its odd-total rejection, half-sum target, initial zero-sum bit, per-value shift-and-OR transition, and target-bit test are exactly the protected app-local algorithm apart from the LeetCode wrapper and annotation.

The legal 4-, 8-, and 16-element even-valued tiers span 4x and make their odd half-target unreachable. The current source passes all 11 executions at +0.03 relative growth and 0.99x; correct uncached include-or-exclude search passes every output but fails only scaling at +4.69 and 877.60x.

The Approach derives the half-total reduction, gives the exact reachable-sum bit invariant, explains why one shift uses each occurrence at most once, and proves the target-bit decision inductively. It states the language-neutral O(nT) time and O(T) space bounds while identifying Python's packed operations.
The hash-bound public Reference retains the complete equal-partition contract, both source examples and explanations in order, both constraints, and the absence of source visuals or tables.
